news.headline: Caterpillar Slides Nearly 5%, Singlehandedly Drags Dow Down 255 Points on Tuesday
news.body: Caterpillar shares fell approximately 4.9% on Tuesday, the steepest drop among Dow components, single-handedly removing around 255 points from the price-weighted index as macro concerns over elevated bond yields and slowing global construction demand weighed on the stock. Twenty of the Dow's 30 components finished higher on the day, yet the index still closed lower—illustrating how heavily weighted industrial bellwethers can distort the headline index reading. The broader S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq lost roughly 1.6% on the session as long-term Treasury yields extended their surge to multi-year highs on inflation fears and heavy AI-related bond issuance. Markets view Caterpillar as a key leading indicator for global capital expenditure cycles, making its sharp decline a cautionary signal for industrial and infrastructure spending outlooks.

news.headline: Fabrinet Crashes 20% on Decelerating Guidance, Dragging Marvell, Amphenol, Coherent Lower
news.body: Fabrinet shares plunged roughly 20% on Tuesday, trading near $476, after the optical manufacturer's Q4 fiscal 2026 beat on revenue of $1.316 billion—up 45% year over year—was overshadowed by decelerating Q1 fiscal 2027 guidance and negative free cash flow of $36.9 million. The sell-off spread across the AI connectivity complex, with Marvell Technology falling nearly 8%, Amphenol down about 7%, Coherent off 12%, and Lumentum dropping nearly 10%. Investors focused on a softer sequential growth implied by the $1.375–$1.425 billion Q1 revenue guide, a $56.7 million loss on non-marketable equity securities, and margin compression. The rout amplified broader risk-off pressure in AI infrastructure stocks alongside surging Treasury yields and reports that Anthropic's ARR came in below investor expectations.

news.headline: Memory Stocks Hit Again: Micron -5%, SanDisk -6%, Western Digital -7% as Rates Bite
news.body: U.S. memory and storage stocks extended their multi-session selloff on Aug. 18 as the 30-year Treasury yield hitting a 19-year high compressed multiples across a sector that had run up 200–650% year-to-date. Micron (MU) fell 5%, SanDisk (SNDK) dropped 6%, and Western Digital (WDC) sank 7%, with Seagate also off 6%; the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) declined ~6%. Analysts flagged the uniformity of declines across names with different product mixes as evidence of a macro rate-driven derating rather than any company-specific deterioration. The group retains extraordinary YTD gains despite the pullback, with Micron still up ~255% and SanDisk up ~653% on the year.

news.headline: U.S. 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits 19-Year High at 5.337%, Pressuring Equities
news.body: The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.337% intraday on Aug. 18 — its highest level since 2007 — before easing to ~5.28%, dragging the S&P 500 down 0.69% to 7,691.76 for a third consecutive losing session and the Nasdaq Composite down 1.33%. The surge reflects a confluence of a worsening U.S. fiscal deficit, record corporate bond issuance (~$1.7T YTD per SIFMA), and rising oil prices as the U.S.-Iran 60-day ceasefire expired without extension. The 10-year yield also climbed above 4.73%, its highest level this year, raising broad financing costs for equities and growth stocks in particular. Markets now await Wednesday's July FOMC minutes, with three dissenters having voted for a hike at that meeting.

news.headline: Bio-Rad Laboratories Tumbles 32% in Volatile Session on Institutional Selling
news.body: Bio-Rad (BIO) crashed 32.4% on Aug. 18 amid heavy institutional selling, technical correction following a sharp short-term run-up, and broader macroeconomic headwinds, according to TheStreet. The move reverses much of the stock's recent recovery after BIO had reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.62 vs. consensus of $1.75 on Aug. 4, when it also announced a restructuring plan. Selling pressure appears tied to profit-taking after a rapid post-earnings surge rather than new fundamental news. The episode highlights the fragility of high-momentum healthcare names in the current rising-yield environment.

news.headline: KOSPI Sidecar Triggered as Index Plunges 6%; Samsung, SK Hynix Each Fall ~7%
news.body: South Korea's KOSPI opened down 5% on August 19 and quickly widened losses to 6.39%, prompting the Korea Exchange to activate the sidecar mechanism suspending program sell orders. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell around 7%, tracking sharp overnight losses in U.S. memory-chip names including Micron and Western Digital on rising bond yields and fading tech risk appetite. The Nikkei 225 fell a concurrent 2.82%, with Kioxia down 9% and Tokyo Electron off 4%, extending a synchronized Asia-Pacific tech selloff driven by surging global long-end yields and Middle East tensions lifting oil prices.

news.headline: Unitree Robotics Surges 542%–629% on Shanghai Star Market Debut, Valued at $66B
news.body: Unitree Robotics, China's best-known humanoid robot maker, opened 629% above its IPO price of 150.80 yuan on the Shanghai Star Market on August 19, briefly hitting 1,100 yuan before paring gains to roughly 968 yuan, giving it a market capitalisation of about 445 billion yuan (~$66 billion). The Hangzhou-based company raised 6.1 billion yuan ($905 million) in an offering that was oversubscribed 8,000-fold — a Star Market record — with strategic backing from DeepSeek and Tencent. The debut makes Unitree the first general-purpose humanoid robotics company listed on a mainland Chinese exchange, coinciding with the opening of the World Robot Conference in Beijing. The listing is being closely watched as a live public-market benchmark for China's fast-expanding humanoid robotics sector, lifting sentiment in related AI and automation stocks across the A-share market.

news.headline: Nikkei Slides 2.5–3.1% as SoftBank Slumps 8%, Kioxia Drops ~10% on Bond-Yield Shock
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell for a second consecutive session on August 19, at one point shedding more than 2,100 points to touch the 65,300 level, as surging global bond yields — with the US 30-year Treasury briefly hitting a 19-year high of 5.33% — crushed risk appetite for high-valuation AI and semiconductor names. SoftBank Group slumped more than 8%, dragged by reports of sluggish OpenAI revenue growth and a 6%-plus overnight drop in its listed subsidiary Arm; memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings fell over 10% intraday before settling around -9%, while Tokyo Electron dropped ~4.4% and Advantest also declined sharply. Japan's own 10-year JGB yield, which touched 2.945% the previous session, added a domestic rate-hike premium to the selling pressure. Markets are now looking to the Bank of Japan's September decision and US Treasury yield trajectory as the key triggers for the next move in Japanese tech stocks.

news.headline: Nvidia H200 Chips Enter Mainland China; ByteDance and Tencent Each Receive ~10,000 Units
news.body: Small batches of Nvidia's H200 AI chips have been allowed to enter mainland China for the first time, the Financial Times reported on August 18, citing two people familiar with the matter. ByteDance and Tencent have each received approximately 10,000 H200 processors in recent weeks, with additional Chinese tech firms expected to secure similar shipments soon. Beijing has stipulated that companies may ship the processors to Hong Kong for use there, as Chinese regulators seek to balance AI competitiveness with support for domestic chipmakers. The development is a positive catalyst for Hong Kong-listed tech names including Tencent (700.HK) and signals a further easing of the H200 import bottleneck.

news.headline: China Tech Earnings Week: Shanghai Composite Rises Ahead of Industrial, Retail Data Dump
news.body: Mainland Chinese shares posted broad gains in early-week trading heading into a key data and earnings window, with the Shanghai Composite adding 1.41%, the Shenzhen Component rising 2.44%, and the tech-heavy ChiNext Index climbing 3.14%, as investors positioned ahead of a slate of Chinese economic releases including industrial production, retail sales, fixed-asset investment, and house prices. The PBOC set its USD/CNY mid-point at 6.7854, a wider-than-estimated fix that tempered some enthusiasm but did not derail the advance. Attention is also on interim earnings from major Hong Kong and mainland internet and consumer names, with the Hang Seng Tech Index up 1.58% on the session, as analysts watch for signals on demand recovery and sector margins. The moves contrast sharply with the semiconductor-led selloff in Japan and South Korea, underlining the divergence between China's domestic policy-driven rally and the broader regional AI-trade deleverage.

news.headline: Brent Tops $91 for Fourth Session as US-Iran MOU Expires, Hormuz Near-Closed
news.body: Brent crude extended its rally to a near three-week high above $91/bbl (WTI ~$85) for a fourth straight session after Trump publicly declared he would not extend the 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding, which officially lapsed Monday. Strait of Hormuz traffic has collapsed to just three vessel crossings in a single day versus ~130 per day pre-war, representing a near-total closure of the waterway that previously carried ~20% of global oil and LNG. A vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the strait on Tuesday, per UK maritime authorities, sustaining engine-room damage and a crew casualty. Saudi Arabia has begun sourcing crude cargoes from outside the chokepoint as Gulf producers seek workarounds, but supply risk remains structurally elevated.

news.headline: Gold Slides $83 as Global Bond Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs, Hormuz Deadlock Bites
news.body: Gold futures reversed sharply on Tuesday Aug 18, settling near $4,390 after opening at $4,473, as the 30-year US Treasury yield climbed above 5.33%—its highest since the 2007 pre-GFC era—and the 10-year approached 4.72%. The broad global bond selloff, driven by fiscal and inflation fears, directly raised the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal; silver also dropped ~3.5% to $63.48/oz. Compounding pressure, the US-Iran MOU expired without extension after Trump explicitly ruled out talks, keeping oil-driven inflation risks elevated. Markets now pivot to Wednesday's FOMC minutes and Fed Chair Warsh's upcoming Jackson Hole keynote for rate-path clarity.

news.headline: US Natural Gas Drops 2% to Near Month-Low on Milder Weather, Storage Build Expectations
news.body: US Henry Hub natural gas futures fell approximately 2% on Monday Aug 17 to around $2.68/MMBtu, their lowest since Aug 7, as updated weather models showed a moderation in heat intensity across much of the country over coming weeks. Reduced expectations for gas-fired power demand for air conditioning are expected to allow storage injections to accelerate, pressuring near-term prices. The pullback comes despite elevated oil prices and Middle East supply risk, highlighting that gas remains driven by domestic weather and inventory dynamics rather than the broader energy crisis.

news.headline: LME Copper Squeeze Hits 2021 Emergency Levels; Stocks Fall 42nd Straight Session
news.body: LME spot copper traded as much as $545/tonne above the three-month contract on Aug 17—the widest backwardation since the 2021 squeeze that triggered LME emergency measures—as warehouse stocks fell for a 42nd consecutive session to 204,975 tonnes, down ~48% since late May and a five-year low. The LME introduced emergency price-cap measures on Aug 14 to limit further spot spikes, with monthly contracts expiring Aug 19 set to test whether the squeeze persists. US copper imports surged to over 200,000 tonnes in July, the largest monthly haul in 12 years, as importers front-ran a pending tariff decision; Jefferies projects a 442,000-tonne market deficit in 2026. Chilean production fell 6.7% YoY through June, and Antofagasta cut annual guidance ~5% after weather disrupted its Los Pelambres mine.

news.headline: Iron Ore Climbs as China H1 Imports Hit Record 628.87 Mt; Vale Shares Rise
news.body: Iron ore proxies rose on Aug 17 after data confirmed China imported 628.87 million tonnes in H1 2026, up 6.3% year-on-year, with June alone at 112.69 Mt (+6.4% YoY)—record-high buying that cushioned sentiment despite tepid property-sector demand. Vale's NYSE-listed shares gained 0.88% to $13.75, though the miner flagged rising costs with C1 cash cost guidance lifted to $22.50–$23.50/tonne. Manufacturing steel demand in China is forecast to grow 3.3% in 2026 to 344 Mt, offsetting construction weakness, but markets remain sensitive to any pivot in Beijing's stimulus posture.
